licensing.additional: No additional HMO licensing scheme: only mandatory licensing, for HMOs with five or more people from two or more households. Planning permission is needed to turn homes into HMOs in parts of the city (Article 4 direction).

housing: Derby has a large stock of Victorian and Edwardian terraces in inner areas such as Normanton, Arboretum and Pear Tree, where private renting and shared houses are common. The University of Derby brings student lets around the Kedleston Road campus and the city centre. Further out are inter-war and post-war suburbs and council-built estates, with large new-build estates on the city's edges.
checkinTips: Victorian terraces in Normanton and Pear Tree: photograph cellars, back yards and any damp on ground-floor walls.
Student and shared houses near the university: photograph each bedroom's lock, furniture and the shared kitchen appliances, and count every key.
Converted mill and office flats in the city centre: photograph ventilation, window restrictors and the communal entry system.
Homes near the River Derwent: note any flood boards or air-brick covers and photograph them in place.
Larger villas split into flats in the Arboretum area: photograph fire doors, door closers and alarms in shared hallways.
tenantHelp: Private tenants with disrepair or safety problems can contact Derby City Council's private sector housing team.
